column3: Hossjer, O. & Gauger, A.K. (2019). A single-couple human origin is possible. BIO-Complexity 2019(1):1-20. doi:10.5048/BIO-C.2019.1
column4: Peer-reviewed journal; independently finds a single-couple origin as recent as ~500 kya compatible with genomic data. Used in Intro and Sec. 4.5 as the independent feasibility anchor.

column3: Swamidass, S.J. (2022). The misunderstood science of genetic bottlenecks. 2022 Annual Meeting / Peaceful Science.
column4: Source of the TMR4A estimate ('median TMR4A ~ 500,000 years'). Verified against the published print. Non-journal venue, attributed as such.

column3: Rogers, A.R., Harris, N.S. & Achenbach, J.D. (2020). Neanderthal-Denisovan ancestors interbred with a distantly related hominin. Science Advances 6:eaay5483.
column4: Peer-reviewed; neandersovan-modern split ~737 ka, ancestor bottleneck Ne~500, direct-scale mutation rate 0.38e-9/site/yr. Anchors the descendant-clade extension and the archaic-branch prediction.

column3: Hu, W., et al. (2023). Genomic inference of a severe human bottleneck during the Early to Middle Pleistocene transition. Science 381:979-984.
column4: Peer-reviewed; FitCoal inference of a severe bottleneck ~930-813 ka (~1,280 breeding individuals). Anchors the SFS-bottleneck literature and the archaic-branch prediction.

column3: Posth, C., et al. (2017). Deeply divergent archaic mitochondrial genome provides lower time boundary for African gene flow into Neanderthals. Nature Communications 8:16046.
column4: Peer-reviewed; provides the published mtDNA-replacement mechanism (gene flow INTO the Neanderthal branch) used by the descendant-clade extension's uniparental boundary.

column3: Tennessen, J.A., et al. (2012). Evolutionary history and adaptation from high-coverage whole-genome sequence data. Science 337:64-74.
column4: Peer-reviewed; Tajima's D = -2.12 (EA) / -2.10 (AA). Replaces the old draft's uncited observed-D claims.

column3: Fenner, J.N. (2005). Cross-cultural estimation of the human generation interval... Am J Phys Anthropol 128:415-423.
Garrigan, D. & Hedrick, P.W. (2003). Detecting adaptive molecular polymorphism: lessons from the MHC. Evolution 57:1707-1712.
column4: Peer-reviewed; MHC recombination/conversion up to two orders of magnitude above genomic average. Anchors the kappa=5 conversion multiplier and the convergent-evolution critique of Ayala's argument.

column3: Tenesa, A., et al. (2007). Recent human effective population size estimated from linkage disequilibrium. AJHG 80:495-505.
column4: Peer-reviewed; observed r^2 in 1-kb bins. Replaces the self-citation for the observed LD target (now stated as the 0.3-0.5 range).

column3: Meyer, M., et al. (2012). A high-coverage genome sequence from an archaic Denisovan individual. Science 338:222-226.
column4: Peer-reviewed; the Denisovan high-coverage genome. Anchors the observed archaic heterozygosity comparison in the archaic-branch prediction.
